utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning. Mr. Registrar, could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Good morning to Your Honours. Good morning to everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case IT-05-88-T, The Prosecutor versus Vujadin Popovic et al. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. For the record, all the accused are present. Prosecution, it's Mr. McCloskey and Ms. Soljan. From the Defence teams, I notice the absence of Ms. Nikolic and Mr. Krgovic. All right. Good morning to you, Mr. Janc.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are going to proceed with your cross-examination today and hopefully finish. Ms. Tapuskovic, good morning to you. Go ahead, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, good morning. Good morning to everyone in the courtroom. Before I start, I would like to tender certain evidence we have used during the examination of expert persons. On the list, Your Honours, you will find ten exhibits. The first five we tender under seal because they contain names; the sixth, not under seal; the seventh, under seal; and the tenth document is MFI. It was submitted for translation. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam. Any objection? Mr. McCloskey? Ms. Soljan? No objection.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, we have no objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. So these documents are admitted as explained by you, some under seal and some -- and one being particularly being MFI'd. All right. Thank you, let's proceed. Incidentally, Mr. Ostojic, I am assuming all along that since you didn't stand you had no documents to tender relating to Dr. Parsons' evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: That's correct, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Mr. Janc, we'll pick up where we left off last Friday. I would only like to add to what I said about 1D362, which contained the information that one of the members of the BH Army was killed on the 18th of August, 1994. And I'd like to answer the question of His Honour Judge Kwon about where that person was and where his body was exhumed from. That individual on your -- is on your confidential Annex B under the heading "Others" and Serbia-related, there are 45 names on the list. And this individual was exhumed in the Zvornik area. Concerning another person mentioned in document 1D1363 [as interpreted], that person is also in confidential Annex B [as interpreted] concerning Bljeceva, more precisely Bljeceva 2. And in the list of missing persons, 494, it says that there is a re-association for that person, but that re-association is related to Bljeceva 2. I hope this answers Judge Kwon's question. Mr. Janc, tell me, have you read the indictment in this case?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You know that in Srebrenica, the 28th Division of the BH Army was stationed, was based?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You told us here earlier about the movement of the column from Jaglici and Susanj; right?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, right.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: On page 33378, on the first day of your testimony in lines 20 to 25, you told us that the sources for your report and your summary were the ICMP list and sources from the competent agencies of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second, Madam Tapuskovic. Before the transcript runs away: Page 2, line 19, that should read 1D1362.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And on page 3, line 2, you said confidential Annex B concerning Bljeceva. Is that correct? I don't see any item on Bljeceva in confidential Annex B. If you could correct me.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: It should be confidential Annex D, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: D, not B.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is confidential Annex D. I might have misspoken. If so, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Very easy to confuse B and D. D for Delta we are talking about. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, Mr. Janc, when you say the competent authorities of Bosnia and Herzegovina, you did not mean the Ministry of Defence, did you?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me whether that decision not to consult the Ministry of Defence and their lists of missing persons and dead during the war in Bosnia and Herzegovina was yours?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Did perhaps the Prosecution suggest to you not to take these lists into account?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they did not.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Does that mean, then, that you did not have insight into what all the Defence teams introduced into evidence on the subject during their respective examinations?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't think that's the case.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Then tell me, what evidence presented by the Defence did you take into account?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't tell you that because I don't have information about all of your evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Did you perhaps take into account 3D398, which is the finding of expert Svetlana Radovanovic led together with annexes during the examination of Drago Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not read her testimony.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. May I now call up 1D1364, but not to be broadcast.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Would you please pay attention to the name of this person without saying it because we can move through all the documents without any problem. Under item 2, you can see that the aforementioned person, as a member of the BH Army, which is stricken, went missing on the 12th of July, 1995. It is then confirmed that the person was born in 1938 in Glogova, municipality of Bratunac, and is on the military evidence of a military unit from the 10th of May, 1992, until 10th January, 1994.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Did the Prosecution perhaps show you this document?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, but it can be found on the system because I see an ERN number, so it's not a problem. I have access to it.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: But have you seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say this particular one, but maybe for some other -- some other individuals.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: We received from the Prosecution about 100 certificates from the Ministry of Defence concerning members of their units submitted to the Prosecution upon their request, and we spoke about this document on Friday, about this type of document. Can you see that it is noted in this document that the certificate is issued concerning a person no longer on the records of the BH Army who was on the evidence of the BH Army from the 10th of May, 1992, and that that person went missing on the 12th of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I now ask the usher to help us and put the document on the ELMO so that it is not available to the public, and to zoom in a little because the script is very small. That is an excerpt from 4494.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: I asked you, Mr. Janc, to pay attention to the name when I showed you that certificate from the BH Army. Do you recognise the person in the middle is the same person named in the certificate of the BH Army?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First name and last names and also the father's name are the same. The date of birth is not.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Correct; date of birth is not the same. But this person is on the list of those identified, and if we can move a little to the right to see where the person was exhumed, we'll see that the site is Kamenica; correct, Mr. Janc?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. You can also see that from the case ID.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Right. And we see from this that this is only a main case; correct? Now, move back to the left, please, to see the status of the case.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. This is the main case.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Since this is an excerpt from the list which I made by cutting off the names above and below, we can conclude that we have no re-association here; correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So I can't say that from this spreadsheet I have in front of me. I would have to consult the entire ICMP update spreadsheet in order to conclude or to give you an answer to that because -- but if you check that, I believe you.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. That's why we made this excerpt including the name before and the name after, to show that it's part of a list. Mr. Janc, if we treat Kamenica as a surface grave - and in your confidential Annex D it is in subfolder Pobudje - can you tell me whether you are able to conclude why in the case of a person found on the surface and for whom there is evidence from the BH Army that they were killed on the 10th of January, 1994, there occurred a change in the date of death and the date of this person's inclusion in the list of individuals identified?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This individual, as I can see here, is not found on the surface. This individual is found in Kamenica 10, which means Cancari number 10 mass grave. If I can move to the beginning, you will see the site code, which is KAM10 Zvornik, so that means Cancari 10. And to comment on your suggestion that there is no re-association in that you have taken this example, I see that it is not in -- just let me see. Okay, you were right. You are right, because I see it is sorted by ICMP ID. Yes. But it is definitely a grave. It's not surface remains.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: All right. This can be verified based on all the evidence you have introduced concerning exhumations. Mr. Janc, it is the Defence case that the Ministry of Defence of Bosnia and Herzegovina had very precise and updated records for their members, and those records showed exact dates of disappearance of their members or their deaths regardless of the cause. Do you know that the lists of the BH Army were the only lists that included unique personal identification numbers, JMBGs?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know that, and I can't see that number from these certificates.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they are not included in the certificates. Do you know, and I suppose you know, that unique personal identification numbers are the most precise identifiers of persons and that even twins have different unique personal identification numbers?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know that that's the case in former Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I now call up 1D1372.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: While we are waiting for this document, this is another cutting from the list of people identified, P4494 made by the Defence, and this document relates to three locations: The first document is location Buk Bijela; the second page is location Bojna; and the third page shows the location Blace, Visegrad. This document should not be broadcast because it contains a name. Mr. Janc, tell me, do you know where these sites are: Buk Bijela; Bojna; and Blace, Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just assume where they are. Like it says here, it's around Foca, the first one. The others are around Visegrad or in Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. If we look at page 1, which shows the location Buk Bljela near Foca, as you said, we ran a check for a person identified here, for the person identified here, and we saw that in the list of people missing from year 2000, which is Exhibit P566; and the list from 2000, P2414; and another list, P3006, we were unable to find this person on the list of individuals identified. Can you tell us, then, why this person now appears on the list of identifications, and why then can he be considered Srebrenica-related if he was not on the list of missing persons?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know why it is on the ICMP list, but I'm sure I did not include this particular person into my report. It's not there and -- yeah, that would be the answer. I don't know why it is on this list because I'm still waiting. I did request the BiH authorities who provided me with the exhumation records regarding these sites as you just mentioned, Foca, Visegrad, all these sites. The request was sent to them, but no response from their side yet, so I'm waiting for these exhumation records to see a little bit more. But it is not included, this person into my report, or this site.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I please move to the next page now.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Having checked all these lists of missing persons that I mentioned earlier, the Defence has established that the person exhumed at Bojna has not been listed in the missing person list, but it is now appearing in this exhibit, which is P4494.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now move to the next page that deals with the Visegrad site. If we can enlarge it, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Before we move on, Ms. Tapuskovic. Mr. Janc, the exhibit we saw earlier on is an excerpt from P4494, which is your confidential Annex D, so I didn't understand that you didn't include them in your report. What did you mean?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I would like to see my report or consult my report regarding that particular individual. But I know, also, for the individuals we can see on the screen now, they are not included in my report. But for that previous one, I'm quite certain that I did not include that particular site in my report. So that's what I know, that I included that particular individual also. So but I would like to see where exactly in my confidential Annex D that individual is listed. Then I can comment a little bit further if you find it, if you find this individual there, but I doubt it's there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I remember I heard from Ms. Tapuskovic that 1D1372 is an excerpt from 4494.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: But it seems to me this is something different because I see -- on the top I see the logo of the ICMP. I don't think these are the same -- the same data they have provided to us and that I have used for my report. If you move up, we will see --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Ms. Tapuskovic, page 8, line 16, you said: "May I now call up 1D1372 ... This is another cutting from the list of people identified, P4494 made by the Defence."

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I'm going to explain it. During my preparations for this cross-examination, the Defence team was using P4494. It's a document done in Excel, which contains 7.762 entries. In Excel, you can sort out the information by any criteria, either by names, columns, location, or any other parameter displayed in 12 columns. Also, by selecting certain parts, you can create an excerpt from that spreadsheet, and all the excerpts that we have been using so far have been made by selecting a specific portion of the list, but we did not realign the order as compared to the original one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ms. Soljan.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd like the Defence to maybe point out where in confidential Annex D that particular ID case can be found because it is not in there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It is your case that that item does not appear in the confidential Annex D?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, just as you pointed out, I would like to ask the question along those same lines.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, you say that these persons do not appear in your Annex D, but in your summary, page 1, you made a note that the number of the identified persons of 5.358 were identified based on the list of identified persons you received from the ICMP. And now I'm going to read it out to you. That is actually page 2 of Exhibit P4490. [In English] "Provided to the ICTY by the ICMP in early March 2009, D000-2768 and by the BH authorities indicates that the remains of at least 5.358 individuals recorded as missing following the fall of Srebrenica have been identified in graves including mass graves, smaller graves, or individual graves to date." [Interpretation] Mr. Janc, the names that I showed you, but we didn't read them out, are the names that appear on the list of the identified persons which you took as a basis for your summary and your annex. But in this part that I read to you on page 2, it is obvious that you have established the number of identified persons based on the document marked D000-2768 entered as P4494, Prosecution exhibit; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We will no longer need this document. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Madam Tapuskovic, do you agree that the person identified on D1372 does not appear in confidential Annex D of Mr. Janc's report?

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I agree, Your Honour, but here I'm talking about the number of persons who were identified, and I'm disputing the number of the identified persons which is linked with the ICMP list entered or admitted into evidence and where these specific individuals are being mentioned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now please see document 1D1371, without being broadcast, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, this is an excerpt made in a similar way from P4494. We have highlighted and selected data by location. The location was Srebrenica hospital, and then we put it on a separate piece of paper. Can you see that? The site name indicates Srebrenica hospital.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, is it possible for us to go into private session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Of course. Let's go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, on page 17, line 7, it says "killed." I didn't say that. In the record on identification the word used was "died," and this is how it wasn't translated into English, as died.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you very much for that remark and correction, Ms. Tapuskovic. Let's proceed. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, we are going to move now to another topic. Can you please tell me what was the situation in Bosnia-Herzegovina regarding the acceptance of identification conducted either by the ICMP or the university clinical centre in Tuzla? In all cases of identification, can you tell me whether the families affected have accepted these identifications?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am afraid I cannot comment on that. I have no such information.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Right. Thank you. Tell me now, are you familiar with the name of Milorad Trbic?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm familiar with it.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You know that his name appeared in the indictment in this case at the time when you started working for the Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You also know that his case has been deferred to the judiciary of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know that.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Did the Prosecutor's Office notify you about the fact that the Prosecutor's Office of Bosnia-Herzegovina issued an amended indictment against him in March of this year?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am aware of that. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can we see Document 1D1360 in e-court, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, did you an opportunity to see that indictment?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR.  MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interject on this, but if she's going to go into the whys and wherefores of charges against Milorad Trbic and open the door to this area, that will open up an incredible amount of information that, you know, the Prosecution will willingly provide, but this is not something at this late stage in the court I don't think anyone wants to get into.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you wish to respond? Are you going to do precisely what Mr. McCloskey is worried about or not? We haven't heard your questions as yet, so we are not in a position to comment and decide on Mr. McCloskey's objection or comment until we either hear your questions or you tell us what your questions are going to be.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, it's absolutely not my intention to go into the substance of this indictment or to discuss it. It is a matter for the authorities of Bosnia-Herzegovina. I just asked the witness if he is familiar with it because I want to ask him a question concerning the annex to this indictment, namely the list of identified persons. As far as the description of charges against Trbic, I don't want to go into that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's proceed for the time being, and then we see.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. To be cautious, I'd like to say the indictment against Trbic is a public document together with the annex, the list of identified persons, but out of an abundance of caution, because some names coincide with our lists, we should not broadcast the documents that we discuss while talking about this annex. Can we now move on to page 15 of this document in English, and I believe it's page 16 in B/C/S. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, do you know that attached to the indictment against Milorad Trbic there is an annex with a list of identified persons containing 3.737 names as noted in the indictment itself and in the last sentence of the indictment where the annex is mentioned?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Soljan.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, before the witness answers, I'd just like a clarification on the meaning of the word "identified." Is this a legal meaning? Is this a meaning as we have it meaning closed case, or are we talking about match reports? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ms. Tapuskovic? What is the -- if you can enlighten us. What is the title of the annex, if it has one?

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if we can go to the indictment itself to see. That's why I suggested to put the indictment in e-court in the first place. At the end of the indictment, it is noted attachment Annex A [In English] 37 identified victims.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't see that. What I see is Annex A to amended indictment, but I don't see any specific title. Date identified, ICRC number. Can -- let me see if I have it at least on here.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If we can go back to the previous page in e-court, which is the last page of the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Can we do that, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we zoom in on the last sentence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I see what you mean. It says what it says. Then it's a question of one's drawn conclusions. That's all. It's indicative that just before it there is an ICRC reference column. Let's continue, Ms. Tapuskovic, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, that's the document as we received it as part of disclosure by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Let's continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, Mr. Janc, did you try to make a comparison between this list of identified persons attached to the indictment against Milorad Trbic, practically for the same events, with the list of identified persons that you attached to your summary?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not, because first time I saw this list was perhaps now ten days ago.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know perhaps, this list of 3.737 identified persons was made based on what?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I understand this list, these are the individuals for which the cases are closed or the individuals are declared dead. What I was using for my report are DNA match reports, which are on the ICMP update, and those is more than just 3.700 as you can see them here. So the ICMP list is more extended because there are also the open cases, which are still running or in process, but this list includes only the cases which are closed.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. May I now call up in e-court 1D1384.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, this is a letter that the Prosecutor's Office of Bosnia-Herzegovina sent to the Defence at the request -- at our request for an explanation how, and based on what, this list of 3.737 identifications was made.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: I'd just like to say that in the original of the document in line 2, it says that this is in fact 3.747 individuals, but the annex to the indictment says 3.737 persons. I will tell you this: [In English] "Annex A is based on certification of that issued by authorised institutions of Bosnia and Herzegovina." [Interpretation] Do you know, Mr. Janc, which are those qualified institutions that issued death certificates?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know, perhaps the court decision or -- I don't know. That's speculation.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. I'll now show you a document made by the Defence team of Mr. Popovic, and it's Exhibit 1D1385. Having the list of identified persons, which is P4494, made in Excel so it can be searched, we tried to make matches between 1449 and the previous document by making an excerpt from that list and taking only main cases -- the exhibit I meant to mention was P4494. Anyway, we made an excerpt by taking only main cases. We removed re-associations, but in the main cases we left all those cases where we have a double name when we supposed that the persons are brothers. This list made in such a way, we matched with the 3.737 names from the Trbic list, that is, the list that the official authorities of Bosnia and Herzegovina accept as the list of identified persons who are their citizens who met their death during the events in Srebrenica. You will see the yellow highlighted name "Trbic" in the left upper corner, and you see the column containing the word "yes," and that means that every person in every horizontal line was matched with the list of identifications that we made, 4494.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now move to document 1D1358A.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You'll see now, Mr. Janc, that this same list is now sorted out by columns, namely whether there was a match or not, and in the first column you have each rubric filled in with the word "yes." We got 5.703 main cases when we made this selection from Exhibit P4494. If we go to the end of this document, you will see that the word "yes" does not feature anymore because these persons were not matched. By reviewing the table, we can see that matches were found for 3.849 persons. Mr. Janc, can you conclude from this whether the real ratio of identified persons in the Srebrenica events can be reflected in a number around 3.000 because these are basically persons who were both by the competent authorities of Bosnia and Herzegovina accepted as identified, and they were also accepted by the families as identified?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Soljan.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, once again, I'd just like it to be made clear whether when Ms. Tapuskovic refers to the real ratio of identified person, identified person meaning closed cases or simply identified as in matched reports obtained by ICMP.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, and who is going to answer that? Who do you expect to be in a position to answer that, Ms. Tapuskovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: I just don't understand when she says identified, whether she's saying --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: She's referring to a document. Let's move on. I mean, and then this can become an argument between you later on if necessary. But I don't expect Ms. Tapuskovic to be able to give you an answer. Perhaps Mr. Janc can, but I doubt it too.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can just say that I don't agree with you. I would only agree if the entire process would be already finished regarding Srebrenica identifications, so the process is still on. So far we have that many identifications, but we expect many more in near future.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Janc, I am going to show you one more document, so can we please now see in e-court document 1D1347.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, this is a letter sent by the government of Republika Srpska to the Defence team providing information required by the Institute For Missing Persons. I think that this was sent on the 18th of August, 2008.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now move to the next page, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, you visited this area in 2007; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, I may be mistaken, you said on that occasion that you visited the Institute For Missing Persons as well.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We were together with them on the field.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. I stand corrected. I'm going to read out to you what they say: "Further to your memorandum of the above number and date, we hereby inform that you the institute had details of 3.214 identified victims of genocide buried in the memorial complex in Potocari and 168 identified victims buried in several local Muslim graveyards. We also have information that the DNA laboratory in Tuzla has completed the preliminary identification of about 2.000 other victims who have still not been identified by their next of kin." Mr. Janc, regardless of the fact, whether it is -- the identification procedure is going on, the fact remains that a certain number of remains, mortal remains, whose identification was established in preliminary terms was not accepted by their families. Am I right in concluding that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Soljan.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Objection, misstating what's in the letter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ms. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no comment, Your Honour. I believe I interpreted the contents correctly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Where do you maintain is the misstatement, Ms. Soljan?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: The letter reads that Tuzla has completed the preliminary identification of about 2.000 other victims who have still not been identified by their next of kin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. That's different from what you say, Ms. Tapuskovic, in alleging that the absence of the identification is due to it not having been accepted by the families.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'm also free to interpret this document myself. If the family does not identify the person, that means that the identification is not accepted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, irrespective of interpretation or not interpretation, could you give us an answer to Ms. Tapuskovic's question, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I do not agree with Ms. Tapuskovic regarding this because what it says here is that these 2.000 victims are still in process. So this has nothing to do with their families.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: But, Mr. Janc, this number of identified persons in the annex to the Trbic indictment, doesn't it tell you that the authorities of Bosnia and Herzegovina do not accept any identifications but the closed cases, that is, those accepted by the families?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Their official number, what they are talking about, is only the closed cases. But what I have used was -- were also the cases which are in process.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Janc, thank you for your answers. Your Honours, I have no further questions of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Tapuskovic. Mr. Ostojic, unless you want the break now and start afterwards?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. We can go for a few minutes if the Court permits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, of course. I was trying to make your life more comfortable.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. It's not that comfortable, but thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Good morning, sir. We have not had the opportunity to meet. My name is John Ostojic, and along with Mr. Predrag Nikolic, we represent Ljubisa Beara in this case. Sir, I'm going to ask you a couple of preliminary questions. First, I'd like to know, is it fair to state that the number of missing persons includes the people who have perished as a result of land-mines, suicide, or the result of legitimate combat engagements in your analysis?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, most probably, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you know what number that is?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know the exact number, but I would say most of the cases are related to the surface remains.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. With the -- including the surface remains, do you know of any evidence - because I know you've read as your addendum, I think, reflected various witness statements and other documents and testimonies in this case - do you know that the number resulting from combat engagements, suicides, and land-mines is roughly anywhere from 1.000 to 2.000?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Would that be reasonable in your view?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Closer to 1.000, perhaps not to 2.000.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Here is what Mr. Butler said -- you know who he is; right?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: He testified on the 23rd of January, 2008, and it starts on page 20212. And we had a little discussion about that with him, but particularly on page 20251, on lines 12 through 14 for my learned friends, in discussing legitimate combat engagements with respect to the Bosnian Muslim military column that was going through Susnjari and trying to make it through Kladanj and Tuzla, he says, quote, in answer to my question: "Yes, sir. I mean, I think the 1.000 to 2.000 number would be reasonable with respect to the combat casualties, starting, you know, from 12 July through the life span of the column which is effectively 18 July."

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you agree or disagree with Mr. Butler's military analytical assessment that the casualties as a result of the military column was anywhere from 1.000 to 2.000?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on the information we have now, I still think it's closer to 1.000.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. And that's based on what, sir?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on the identifications we have for surface remains, which is 648 now.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, you spoke about a region called the Pobudje region; correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Pobudje region.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Pobudje region. Within that region, am I correct that the areas that are found in that region are Ravni Buljim, Kamenica, Sandici, and Konjevic Polje?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is area from Ravni Buljim up to Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you also, sir, know from your investigative duties that in those four that I've just mentioned - Ravni Buljim, Kamenica, Sandici, and Konjevic Polje - those were four sites of actual combat engagements that the VRS engaged with the Bosnian Muslim military column. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, with respect to that specific region, if you will, how many people from the statements that you reviewed perished within that region based on those combat engagements?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, let's take a look at some of those witness statements briefly.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Let's call into e-court, if we can, 2D667, and If we can just, please, have the first page because I do have a couple of questions on the first page. Oh, you know, I'm sorry. If I could just restate the number. It's a different exhibit. It's 2D669. I'll be using 2D667 a little later.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, I just want to point this out to you for the record. This is a statement taken by the ICTY investigators, and we can see there was a statement taken approximately six months after the events of Srebrenica in July of 1995, namely on the 19th of January, 1996, and it was taken by -- at one point, it was the lead investigator, Mr. Ruez. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: This is a statement that I think should not be broadcast because of the individual's name, and I'm just not sure if we're authorised to just use it without his permission. But in any event, this is a statement that was taken shortly after the events, and I want to point out the first page, which is page 2 of this document, the witness statement, and I ask you, have you reviewed this witness statement at all in preparation of your report or any evidence that you may be giving at any time?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps I have, but I can't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, if you see in the middle of that page where it starts with witness statement, it talks about the column started to move the next day at 0100 hours. Do you see that in the centre?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And he continues to discuss that they went over the Buljim mountain and arrived at Jaglici at 0500 hours. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, is that in the Pobudje area, region?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is in Pobudje region, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And then if we look at the last paragraph in this page, he says he was moving towards the front when a very strong shooting started again, coming from all kind of weapons. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if we flip to the next page, he discusses that he saw - thank you - on the first line, that he saw many dead bodies around, and, also, many wounded who had limbs cut due to the shelling. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, did anyone try to find out from this witness how many dead he saw as a result of this combat engagement?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, but I'm also skeptical how he could tell us this thing, how many of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, because he was there and he saw it. He observed it. He was part of it. He experienced it. That would be some way to tell us, wouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but the total numbers, you know, are always -- you have all of these doubts about their accuracy because it's not that easy to establish how many people is gathered, for example, in one place.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, do you know that actually this witness, they did ask him how many people he saw, and he said 2 to 3.000. Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Well, let me point it out to you. On the fourth page of this document, this witness discusses another engagement having come back to the Buljim region or the Buljim area, and he says there was another combat engagement. If we could just -- it's on the bottom of page 4. I'm kind of just skipping around, but you're welcome to look at the whole document at the break or at any time. He says: "We then arrived in the forest where the second ambush occurred in order to try to identify some body. Bodies were still all around. I recognised bodies of two men who were with me at the beginning, at their clothes and their bags." Now, the next paragraph is really what I want to ask you about before the break. He says also further --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yes, next page. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yes, just to get this question out and then -- I realise that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: "We did not count the bodies we saw, but I would estimate that there were about 2 to 3.000 bodies." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I guess it's the break, but I'll follow up on that at the break. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. We will have a break now of 25 minutes' duration. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Incidentally, before we proceed, we are sitting pursuant to Rule 15 bis this morning. Judge Prost couldn't be with us. Thank you. Mr. Ostojic, you may proceed, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, is there any reason that you know of that we should doubt what this witness on Exhibit 2D669 had reported to the ICTY investigator in January 1996?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. First of all, we have the number of surface remains collected in this area, and you can find the total of them. It's a little bit more than 500 in this Pobudje area so far identified, which you can find it in my report. Second, I'm wondering how accurate this number is. In order to assess the number you need some special, I would say, training. It's not that easy. As police officer, I can say that there is a special training in order to assess how many people is gathered, for example, in one place. So -- and if you are not trained in that, so you can be -- you can be wrong easily.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Well, what --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. Do you have a problem? Mr. Borovcanin, Mr. Nikolic? It's okay? No if you have a problem, speak up. All right. Thank you. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, what endeavours did the Office of the Prosecution take in order to determine out of the numbers that you've put in your report, the 5.300 or so, how many were actually as a result of casualties from walking over land-mines? Did you do that analysis?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you know of anyone who did at the Office of the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think no one did it.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. How about did anyone do an investigation or at least undertake the process to determine how many people from this military column that was leaving from Susnjari, how many died as a result of self-inflicted wounds or suicide?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there were no such investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. How about as a result of these legitimate combat engagements? When the VRS attacked the legitimate column of military men, did anybody investigate to determine how many actually died as a result of that combat engagement?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware of any such investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Not doing any of the investigation on at least those three and other areas, did you investigate whether or not any of those people who died as a result of either suicide, mines, land-mines, or combat engagements, whether anyone buried those individuals?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, I was trying to find that fact, but there were instances regarding this Glogova, what I mentioned with my corrigendum, but apart from that there were not a lot of such information.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: We did look at the evidence relating to Glogova and the Kravica warehouse, and we're familiar with those facts, but with respect to any other site, is it fair to state that no such investigation was conducted or undertaken to determine whether or not the people within the graves that were found - not just surface remains, sir - were actually casualties as a result of land-mines, suicide, or combat engagements?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think that no investigation was done regarding that. We have a lot of expert reports regarding the mass graves, and what are their conclusions, you can find there.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I've looked at that, and I think you gave us a double negative which makes it unclear for me. What do you mean when you say "I don't think that no investigation was done ..."?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That I'm not aware of.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, are you aware of the United Nations report dated the 17th of July, 1995, by a Mr. Ken Biser?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I've seen this report, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Have you included this at all in any part of your analysis?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Let's bring it up, please. And I've got to find the exhibit number. Sorry. I usually write the exhibit numbers on the actual exhibit. I failed to do it on this one. Forgive me. It's 1D374. Thank you, and I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Is this the report you are referring to, sir? Do you see it, July 17th, "from" on the right-hand side in the second box?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, if we could flip to the second page of this document. And here, Mr. Biser is reporting based on the information that he collected, because we are talking about what they knew contemporaneous to the events, if you will. He says under paragraph number one, third bullet point, is what I'd like to focus on. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: He says: "Up to 3.000 were killed on the way, mostly by mines and BSA engagements." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, what did the Office of the Prosecution, you being an investigator there, do to determine or rule out that fact?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not ruling out that fact that this has happened, but the problem here is how many of them were indeed killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: But if we want to be fair and objective taking your number of 5.000 plus, of those 5.000, 3.000 based on evidence from this witness statement and others that we have that we'll show you, as well as the United Nations person here, he says that up to 3.000 were killed on the way from two sources, mines, and he says BSA, which is the Bosnian Serb Army, engagements. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you have any evidence to dispute that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We have evidence how many of them have been found on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Just surface remains?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Surface remains, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, what about those in the graves, the multiple graves that you found?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The biggest grave in that area is Glogova grave, and we know through various witness statements which bodies were buried there, so I am not aware of any other mass graves in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Well, look at -- it also goes on in this document that will be dealt with that some committed suicide. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you know how many?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you know the manner in which suicide was committed by the Bosnian Muslims in that column?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you know that the statements in the possession of the Prosecution indicate that there were various methods as well as falling on top of a grenade and turning the grenade on?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know for that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, what other means do you know of, sir?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are the main that you mentioned now.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I only mentioned one. What other means were there?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that there was also instances where they hanged themselves, or else --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: How about self-inflicted wounds from a pistol or a gun?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think I do remember those also.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Of course. And when you look at the autopsy reports or the pathology reports when they identify cause of death and manner of death, they describe it as a wound to the skull or to the temple area. Now, can you exclude, sir, or did you try to exclude the possibility that the person who the pathologists have identified as sustaining a bullet wound to the head died as a result of suicide?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Just based on that, you cannot exclude that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Can you exclude, sir, when you find other manner or causes of death as bullets on a body or a corpse, if you will. That it was as a result of legitimate combat engagement because there was an exchange of fire?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So depends how many of those have indeed been found there with the same wounds or in the grave.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And I agree it does. I don't have the burden of proof. The pathologist certainly testified here, as I'm sure you are aware. Out of the 5.000 plus, 5.300 plus that you've identified, is there any reason, sir, that you can think of with the exception of Glogova, which we talked about, and the Kravica warehouse that we read your addendum with respect to that and the number that you identified there, is there any reason why we cannot include and adopt the figure; although Mr. Butler says it's 1 to 2.000, this witness says he saw 2 to 3.000, the UN reported on the 17th of July that it was up to 3.000, that in your list up to 3.000 if not more - and I suggest to you more - are included in the numbers that you're providing for us in this report?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't agree with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Why not, if you didn't do the analysis to determine that or rule it out?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because the reports from the exhumations and the reports done by the experts shows the opposite, so that they were -- these people were killed, and also, evidences found inside these graves are related or linked with the execution points.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you know, sir, that the pathologists were unable to rule that out?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you can't rule that out in 100 per cent.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, let's talk about your page 35 and 36 of your report where you list these execution sites and the graves that you found. Do you have that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, the first one you identify as an execution site at Kravica; correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And how many graves do you identify there, 16 under that section?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Well, did you try to determine whether or not in any of the graves other than Glogova 1 and 2, whether or not those graves are resulted from the buried men and victims as a result of either land-mines, suicide or legitimate combat engagements?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Well, if it's true what this witness said and other witnesses that you've interviewed, your office, if it's true what Mr. Butler said, and if it's true what the UN report identifies, up to 3.000, where do you think those men were buried if we know that there were combat engagements in the Pobudje region in Ravni Buljim, Kamenica, Sandici, and Konjevic Polje? Where do you think those people were buried?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think most of them just stayed there.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Based on what? Based on your interviews with the witnesses or based on speculation?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's not speculation. The burial process in the -- in the Glogova was finished up to 17, most of it. So we have only two graves after the 17 of July. So grave E and grave L where we have in total 18 victims, so most of the work was done by 17 of July. So based on the information and witness statements and their testimonies here in this courtroom, most of these -- most of the victims buried in Glogova are coming from Kravica.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. And I did I think say, and forgive me if I didn't, let's take Glogova out to the side for one second. I know you want to talk about it, and I recognise what you've done in Glogova, but with respect to the other grave sites, I'm saying you did not do anything to determine or evaluate whether or not based on the fact there were at least four and possibly five combat engagements in that area, the Pobudje region, that you didn't determine whether or not those people buried in those graves were casualties as a result of this legitimate combat engagement or other means. You didn't rule it out, isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, the same can be said for the next region which I think you have identified or I thought it was the next -- was the Udrc, U-r-d-c [sic]. I'm having very trouble this morning, sorry. U-r-d-c. You know there was an ambush there as well?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Are you familiar with what region that belongs to?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean in my report?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Just generally, do you know in what region based on your analysis does this fall in?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the region I would say next to or close to Pobudje. Just across the road is Udrc.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: How about Snagovo? What region does that belong to?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's south-west of Zvornik, so it is between Udrc and Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Are you familiar with whether or not there was an ambush at Snagovo?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. There was. Are you aware of an ambush at Orahovac?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Are you aware of an ambush at Baljkovica?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you know how many people died in all of those ambushes, sir, as a result of legitimate combat engagements?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not easy to establish how many.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Well, can you give us a best estimate as opposed it to a precise figure?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you know if any of the people who died as a result of those legitimate combat engagements, mines, or suicide in those other ambushes, whether or not they're included in your report?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that because I don't have their names.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Well, let me ask you about that. You think really that the families of the victims whether they died or perished as a result of execution or legitimate combat engagement or suicide or land-mines, do you think when they reported that they were missing they were able to tell you what their manner of death was?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I think not.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Of course not, because they just know that they're missing. So they don't know how, where, or when they died. That was really your job, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, part of it, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, we know from some of the evidence that we heard that there were, I think, and I don't mean to misstate it, but I think that there were two specific graves where there were a significant amount of ligatures found at or around the grave-site or on the particular bodies or on the corpses of the individuals that were exhumed. Are you familiar with that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, that is an indication, you'll agree with me, of an execution, wouldn't you?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you know what the total number of those corpses or victims were and the graves where there were actually evidence of ligatures and blind-folds? Do you know what that total is?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not from the top of my head. I would have to consult Dean Manning's reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Do you know it's roughly anywhere between 5 and 700? Would that sound accurate to you?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Ostojic, could you kindly slow down --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I will. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- and allow a short pause between question and answer. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, sir, let's go back to your report on page 36. Do you have it?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Going back to the Kravica section where you identify 16 graves.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, we talked about Glogova, and other people will ask you specifically relating to that. The balance of these graves, when you bold the name, does that mean it's a primary grave?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you repeat? What do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yeah, sure. Like, we see Glogova 1 and 2 as being bold; Ravnice 1 is bold; Zeleni Jadar 5 and 6 are bold; the balance of them are not bold.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These bolded ones were exhumed by the ICTY.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Now, with respect to the graves that you found other than Glogova that were exhumed and investigated, if you look at the numbers, the numbers are the people who were identified that were found in the graves; correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did you ever go back to try to determine knowing that the numbers were identified to match to determine if these people died, based on either the pathology report or witness statements or any other sources you may have, as to whether or not they died in the manner of death of land-mine explosions, suicide, or legitimate combat engagements?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, but this can be done.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: How long would it have taken you to do that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think a lot, but -- and I also doubt that I'm a proper expert to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, who would be? Because you said earlier, I thought, that it's the person who saw and experienced and was in the column, he probably was wrong in his estimate, but it takes an expert to do it, such as yourself. Who other than you would be able it to do that analysis?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps a pathologist.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did you ever review the material with respect to where the land-mines were in the area, particularly as it may relate to the route that the Bosnia Muslim column took from Susnjari?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know I am aware of one at Ravni Buljim or around that place.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. And then --

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were also others, but I cannot remember now.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Who did that analysis for the OTP as to where the land-mines were and their locations?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I do remember these places mentioned by the survivors.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Let's look at your P2110, please, and with the Court's permission, we'd ask the usher's assistance because I'm going to have him possibly mark this exhibit for me. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, this, sir, is a map I think that you drew up showing the route of the Bosnian Muslim column.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If we could just enlarge it if you don't mind. I think they're both the same, so we just need to have the one, if it's permissible, in either language. It should be the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did you make this map, sir?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, I didn't. This map was prepared by Jean-Rene Ruez and used during his testimony, I guess.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Well, I want to stick to these regions that you've helped us identify and the Pobudje region, which includes obviously Kravica and several of the other places like Kamenica, Ravni Buljim, Sandici, and Konjevic Polje. Can you, with the Court's permission and the assistance of the usher, circle that region for me?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And if you don't mind putting there PR so that we'll know it's the Pobudje region.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: PR.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yeah, P for Pobudje and then R for region. Would that be okay?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Inside?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Anywhere you'd like.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, where was the ambush -- or then VRS engagement, combat engagement at Ravni Buljim? Do you see that on the map? Just put an X on it.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, it's close to I think Jaglici or somewhere here.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yeah, just put an X.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And how about Kamenica? Where was that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Kamenica is close to Kravica. Should I put it --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yeah, you can put a Y for that.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: How about Sandici?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here is Kamenica, and Sandici, I put it S. It's around Sandici.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. And how about Konjevic Polje?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's up here in Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Is that part of the Pobudje region?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm calling the Pobudje region, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, within those four areas where those ambushes or engagements occurred, do you know how far the distance is from the graves that you cite in your report on page 36, the 16 or so that we've seen, do you know the distance from where these combat engagements occurred and where the graves are?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We know Glogova is very close to Kravica.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yeah, we know.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Then, also, Ravnice is up there close to Glogova above Kravica. And then we have secondary graves Bljeceva and Budak, so for Bljeceva they are left of Srebrenica where you can see -- no, sorry. Potocari. They are left of Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 1, 2, and 3, and also --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: How about Zeleni Jadar?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And also Budak ones are here. And then we have down on the map you can see Zeleni Jadar, and they are around -- all of those same graves is down there.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Can you put a ZJ for Zeleni Jadar, please.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, going to the next region keeping with this map which you have as an execution site, but I wanted to ask you actually about Udrc. Where is that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Udrc is -- I'll make a circle.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Should be here somewhere. I'll put U for Udrc.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Very logical. Thank you for that. And how about Snagovo? Where is that region, if you will, because that's where a combat engagement occurred as well.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. So I'll mark it like area here, up there.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: How about Orahovac? What was that region? We have evidence there was a combat engagement there as well.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This region I would call Baljkovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. So you're calling Orahovac and Baljkovica the same region?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Fair enough. Just so we can understand it. And you know there were at least two ambushes, one at Orahovac and one at Baljkovica. You're familiar with that, I think, you've said; correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Just circle that area that we'll called Baljkovica, and identify it, please, with a B.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And I think Snagovo you did not identify, but if we could use SG because you've already used the letter S for Sandici. That might be -- help us later.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, based on these four regions, if you will, I think, do you know what the closest grave was vis-a-vis the combat engagement? That is, the combat engagement happened, let's say, at Konjevic Polje. What was the closest grave-site near or around Konjevic Polje that was exhumed?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We having Konjevic Polje itself, and Nova Kasaba, several graves.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did you take into account in your analysis or your review that the people buried in those graves may have been, probably were, casualties as a result of legitimate combat engagement?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so in these graves, like I mentioned, in or around Nova Kasaba that we have those cases because we have -- they have been some of them ligatured and found in these graves.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Which -- where were the two graves found where there was a predominant amount of evidence and ligatures and blindfolds? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I would like to consult the report, but I think Nova Kasaba, 1996 and 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Any others?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this area or Nova Kasaba specifically?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: In any area.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We have also in Cerska.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: What region does that belong to?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is the region close to Udrc.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: What other area?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think we have in the northern part those cases, also, which is around Orahovac and Kozluk and Brano.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, whose job is it, sir, to rule out that in those graves where you found the corpses that they were not part of the victims who suffered as a result of these legitimate military combat engagements? Whose job do you think that is?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For example, pathologist, forensic pathologist, those kind of experts.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: My question was a little broader. It's -- first of all, you don't dispute with me that it's the job of the Prosecution and the investigators to rule that out and to exclude that; correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Because, why, you carry the burden of proof?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. It's not my job, but I can I sure you of that. Now, what did you or anybody that you know of based on your knowledge do to exclude that probability, that within the numbers of 5.300 plus that you're offering, that in fact 3.000 plus or so are part or not part of that report?
