What steps did you take?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Me personally, I cannot tell you, but I think --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, you personally -- oh, sorry. You personally didn't do anything, right, with respect to that issue, so you could tell us.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: With respect to that issue, perhaps not, but I have reviewed a lot of these reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: As I understand that. I'm not taking that away from you. I'm sorry for overlapping. But you personally didn't. I'm asking, do you know of anyone else who did? We know what Mr. Butler said in this vein, and he said he was unaware of anyone conducting that type of analysis or process. Do you know of anyone who did or may have?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. If you could just sign or initial the bottom and date it, of this exhibit, P2110, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And thank you, Madam Usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If we could save that document, Mr. President, I'd appreciate it, or whoever. And now I'd like to turn to another exhibit, which is P4500. It's identified as a "tracking chart for Srebrenica cases."

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, do you have the document in front of you?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Who created this document?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think this is ICMP document.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Did you rely on this document at all in your analysis, or in your report?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because I was using their data, list of data they have provided to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Particular DNA match reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you know what the position is of Mr. Parsons from the ICMP as to the reliability of this document?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not really.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. I wasn't sure if you were listening to some of his testimony. That's why I ask. Look at the total section of this document. Do you see it down towards the bottom of the page?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And if we could highlight or enlarge that, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you see the number of bodies buried that they identify?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: How could you reconcile that number with the number that you report of 5.300 plus in your report?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same answer as before. These are closed and completed cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. And this was as of April 10th, 2009, this report, is it not?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, if we can look at another exhibit which was in your, I think, Annex B of your report, which is the DNA connection chart. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: DNA connections are Annex D.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And it's the last page of that report, I think, of that annex.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So if we can please have up on the e-court, the last page of annex --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: C.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: C.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: As they are bringing it up, I'll ask you this, since you have it in front of you, sir. Who created this chart?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not yet in front of me, but this chart was created by our analyst.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, I know it's not on the e-court, but you turned to the page in your report, and you have it in front of you, right? You have it physically from your report. I see it; right?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now we have it on the e-court as well. What analyst created this chart?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The analyst from our team, Panayota Vassou.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: With respect to this chart, sir, can you just help me understand it just a little bit better when you try to identify. Like, you say it's DNA and forensic evidence connections. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Is the bottom section, if we take the left-hand side, and you see that it's Cancari Road mass graves; do you see that, the box captioned that way?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And they have instances where they identify, for example, 24 cases in between Cancari Road 12 and Cancari Road 11. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, how -- above that immediately where they talk about the soil and pollen samples, blind-folds and ligatures, do you see that section?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: They identified 20 cases in the red right-hand side of that little area. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: What does that mean, 20 cases?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 20 cases mean that we have 20 connections, DNA connections between Branjevo farm and Cancari Road secondary mass graves.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: 20 out of how many?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you help me find the --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I'm sorry. I tried to walk you through it. It's on this exhibit on the left-hand side. If we go from the beginning where it says "DNA and forensic evidence connections," immediately below that is a box which says "Branjevo farm (Pilica)." Immediately below that, we see a 6 figure with a blue and red mark showing the pollen and soil samples, and right below that there's the words "20 cases," and it's on the left-hand side on the top half.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Proceed, Mr. Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And I'm sorry, sir. I missed your answer on that. What does the 20 cases mean?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That you have 20 connections between Branjevo Pilica farm -- Branjevo farm and Cancari Road.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry. I thought my question was out of how many, and I didn't get that answer. 20 cases out of how many?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You know, it's not easy to say because the connections are different, as I explained already, than actual identifications, so I don't know out of how many, but I would have to consult the DNA -- the ICMP update regarding this to see how many cases is in Branjevo in all, in total.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: About in total how many were on the Cancari Road mass graves?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same answer. I would have to consult.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And would your same answer be -- would your answer be the same as a result for each one of these sections, like Kozluk and the Cancari Road mass graves as well as Lazete and the Hodzici Road mass graves, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. The answer would be the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So just explain to me, what's the purpose of this chart, or what are you trying to establish?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The purpose of this chart is to show, to present how many DNA connections we have between primary and secondary graves, between primary and primary graves, and secondary, secondary graves. So how many bodies or part of the bodies have been found, of one individual have been found on two different locations.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Ostojic, when we have the chart in front of us, so let's take a look at Cancari Road mass graves. Am I correct in reading that there's no DNA connection in relation to Cancari Road 1, 4, and 8?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes, you are correct. Cancari Road 1 is not exhumed yet. Cancari Road 4, 6, and 8 were just recently exhumed, so we are waiting for first results from the ICMP. So that's most probably why we don't have any connections between these graves.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: May I proceed, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. But in your Annex A, Cancari Road 4, Kamenica 4, you said -- you referred to DNA profiles, unique profiles?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. For Cancari -- we have for Cancari Road 4 the unique DNA profiles already, yes, some of them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So which means that there has been found no DNA connection whatsoever in relation to that grave?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not yet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: What do you mean by "not yet"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because the process is still ongoing. As you can see here, we have only ten, ten unique profiles so far identified from Cancari Road 4, so the process is still going on. And probably with next update, we'll have much more results regarding these three sites which were exhumed by the end of last year.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm going to move away from this document, Honourable Judge Kwon, so I don't know if you needed any further ...

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, can I show you now 2D702, and it should not be broadcast because, again, it's a witness statement from an individual who we did not obtain express permission to utilise, so in the abundance of caution we should not broadcast that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are being informed that it's not in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: It was sent subsequently as an addendum to the exhibit list, but I do have a hard copy if the witness would like to look at it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think that will make --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Before I started my cross --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In the meantime, it will hasten things up, speed a things up.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I think she should show it to the Office of the Prosecution because there are some markings on it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Show it to the Prosecutor, please. Do you have any objections, Ms. Soljan, with using it?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: No, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. So let's put it on the ELMO and proceed, and in the meantime we'll check whether it has turned up in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Just the first page first, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, that's another witness statement that was given by a person who was in the military column, and it was given to the ICTY investigators, and it's a little more contemporaneous to the date of the events than the prior statement we saw in January of 1996, is it not?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: In fact, this one is one month or so after the events, August 23rd, 1995; right?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you're right.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did you review this statement and the other tens and I think hundreds of statements from Bosnian Muslims who reported the ambushes and the number of individuals who died as a result of legitimate combat engagements?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if we could turn to the fourth page of this document, I believe, and it's highlighted in green.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: This witness says that during an ambush that he witnessed, observed, that 500 men were killed as a result of legitimate combat engagement.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Maybe I could look at the document and point directly where I believe it is. Thank you, Madam Usher.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And it's -- I highlighted it and put -- do you see that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Well, did you take this -- is there a -- strike that. Was there any reason that you know of or that you found that we cannot reasonably rely on this statement given to the ICTY in August of 1995 of this individual?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We can rely on the -- on his statement, but, you know, again, it's the question of the accuracy of the number.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: We know that, and you've said that, but you've done nothing and you know of no one at the Office of the Prosecution who did anything to determine the accuracy of the number; isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In part you are right.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, let's quickly look - thank you for that, I'm done with that document - at 2D667, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, I'm not showing you all the witness statements. I just want to make sure to tell everyone I'm not going through all the witness statements that are on EDS with respect to these issues, but there are literally hundreds. So 2D667. Again, sir, as it's coming up, it's a witness statement from a Bosnian Muslim who was in the military column from Susnjari; statement was given on the 9th of June, 1999, to the ICTY.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. What I'd like to do is to turn to page 4 of that document, and it's the third full paragraph where it begins: "Around 1400 hours ..." Do you see that? And it's the really the last sentence of that paragraph that I wanted to ask you about. It says: "Some of the people, there were approximately ten of them, who did not want to surrender, committed suicide. I saw them lie down and put hand-grenades under their stomach. They blew themselves up." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Based on your review, if you had done it, do you know how many people committed suicide who were on the Bosnian Muslim column once they left Susnjari?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, because we don't have in possession all of the autopsy reports regarding these surface remains, so we can't say anything about it, so I don't have any information.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And when do you expect out of those 500 or so, I think you said, surface remains that you would get the information from the autopsy or pathologist?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Did you review the pathology reports as to the cause and manner of death of the bodies that they did identify?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, some of them, but not all of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Excluding Kravica and Glogova, and excluding the two sites where we saw a significant amount of ligatures and blind-folds, do you agree with me that the cause and manner of death identified by the pathologist is vague?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't comment on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, why not? You're an investigator. You gave them the direction to provide that information. If they say someone died as a result of a bullet wound, does that answer the question as to whether or not that person died from a self-inflicted wound, a wound from one of his colleagues, a wound from a combat engagement, or a wound from an executor? All those four or five possibilities exist, do they not?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they do, but now in order to -- to clarify the issue, you have to look into this particular case from different perspectives. You have to find more, for example, information about this particular individual; not only the reports, also the information statements and whatever evidence you can find on this person, and then you can maybe perhaps establish the manner and cause of death.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So are you saying, sir, that in fact you think it may not be vague but that it's incomplete?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, try to be more definitive. You're an investigator giving evidence in an International Criminal Tribunal. You made a report in this case. Not perhaps; it's without a doubt, isn't it, that the path report does not exclude or rule out any of the possibilities that I'm suggesting that the numbers that you've given us are indeed inflated and include individuals who died as a result of sustaining injuries from land-mines, self-inflicted wounds, and/or injuries from legitimate combat engagements.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you're right.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Bourgon?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: I have no questions at this time, Mr. President. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Bourgon. Mr. Lazarevic? Lectern, please. How long do you estimate the duration of your cross-examination, Mr. Lazarevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I assume it will take more than one hour and a half, a bit more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The rest of the day, probably.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Anybody else cross-examining the witness? Ms. Fauveau?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No more than 10 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So we should make an effort to finish with the witness today. I think it is still possible unless there is a re-examination. Mr. Haynes I think last time reserved his position, but wasn't quite ...

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Yes. I mean, Mr. Ostojic has stolen a good deal of my thunder, but I will take some instructions at the next break. It's likely I will take five or ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. So it's not likely that we finish your testimony today then. We'll continue tomorrow because we have barely an hour and a half or just less than that. Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Janc. Good morning to everyone in the courtroom. My name is Aleksandar Lazarevic, and together with my colleagues from the Defence team, I represent Mr. Borovcanin in the case before this Tribunal, and I will be putting questions to you on his behalf. I understand that you understand and speak B/C/S very well. You will understand my questions without interpretation and will not need to wait for it. Let us make an effort, therefore, to avoid answering too soon or overlapping. Can we now begin?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we can.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Janc, from your supplemented summary, P4490 together with the confidential annex with a different number, I concluded from the cover page that it was submitted on the 13th [Realtime transcript read in error, "15th"] of March, 2009; correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Sorry, let me correct the transcript. I said 13th of March, not 15. Your colleagues from the OTP, did they have an occasion to familiarise themselves with the contents of your summary before it was disclosed to the Defence?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me, who was the person in the Office of the Prosecutor who reviewed your summary before it was disclosed to the Defence?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have sent it to Ms. Soljan and Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Soljan and Mr. Vanderpuye, when they reviewed your summary and before it was disclosed to the Defence, did they have any comments or critique, namely that some allegations are inaccurate or incomplete or that they do not reflect the Prosecution case on a certain issue?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there were not such comments. There were some comments regarding the grammar and spelling and these kind of issues, and also there were discussion regarding the issue how to present the DNA connection part in writing. Such discussions were going on, but there were no other instructions.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So in terms of accuracy and precision and the position of the OTP regarding your work, there were no changes, no objections from the persons from the OTP you have just named?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, because initially before I started preparing the report, there were discussions what areas my report should cover. That was all. And then I've prepared the report, and then just these final comments which I have just mentioned. That was all.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So you had received from the OTP instructions as to the -- what your report should contain, if I understood you correctly; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's more precisely to say, you know, which areas should cover. The main issue was to present the updated numbers regarding the new exhumations, new identifications, and surface remain sections, and also there were discussions regarding these DNA connections, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So you received instructions in that sense by telling you, Mr. Janc, keep to what we want you to represent in your report. Is that how it was? Seems that there are already some mistakes in the transcript, so I'll repeat my question. You had received as an instruction to stick to what the topic of your report was going to be. You were told, in other words, that this is going to be the topics of your work and that you should abide by that.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we can say something like that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: After submitting your basic summary on the 13th of March, 2009, on the 9th of April you submitted a corrigendum to this same summary, and we had an opportunity to see this document, which is number 5492, and it was shown to you by Ms. Soljan. I just wanted to specify the time-line and the dates of the -- my apologies, it's document P4492. In any case, this corrigendum was submitted on the 9th of April of this year; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me, did you draft this corrigendum on your own after you had reviewed again your basic summary, or was it someone from the OTP who asked you to do it?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Actually, both. I was already aware of this mistake, and I have plans to prepare corrigendum. There were also discussions later on with these same individuals from the OTP that this should be done.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So it means that knowing the content of your corrigendum, and we are going to discuss it later on, you yourself had noticed that some of your statements in the basic summary practically did not reflect the state of facts or the position of the OTP vis-a-vis certain issues.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. When I was reading your motion, and you pointed that out, I did remember this thing, although I was aware of that before, but I did mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: At any rate, tell me -- well, it means that you established this yourself, and after that Ms. Soljan and Mr. Vanderpuye practically gave you identical instructions in terms that these sections need to be corrected; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Actually, they have asked me what is my opinion and what do I think about this particular issue, and I explained what is my position, and I also explained that I would prepare a corrigendum.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Did they tell you specifically in what way should this corrigendum be drafted?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they did not tell me because I think I did understand the point.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: When you spoke to Ms. Soljan and Mr. Vanderpuye and when you discussed the corrigendum, were you told that Mr. Borovcanin's Defence was going to refute your conclusions contained on page 60 in B/C/S and 41 in e-court? Were you also told that the Borovcanin Defence already had drawn the OTP's attention to that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they have told me that, yes, also, but they did not show me the actual correspondence between yourself.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Was that also the reason for you to decide to change the corrigendum in light of the statement of the Defence to the effect that they were going to change certain -- or challenge certain statements in your summary? I'm sorry, another correction. I already misspoke when I said change the corrigendum. I meant for to you change your basic summary.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't think so. I would prepare the corrigendum also without these facts.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please now look at document P4424. That's the map that we had already saw. I'm sorry, the number is P4524.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: This is -- or actually, these are the maps with the markings that you personally put on them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And if we can just look at the bottom part of this map. Can we please look at the bottom part of the map showing Kravica, Glogova, Ravnice, and Zeleni Jadar.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, bearing in mind your corrigendum, and you know what it contains, is there an arrow missing on this map connecting Bratunac and Glogova, since in the corrigendum you said that the bodies from the school in Bratunac were also buried in Glogova.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, perhaps it should be there also. I agree with you, but no -- yeah, perhaps it should be there also.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. And, of course, also based on your corrigendum there should be an arrow linking Konjevic Polje and Glogova as well; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the same. You're right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And, of course, the same applies to an arrow that should connect Potocari and Glogova, and the Bratunac-Konjevic-Polje road and Glogova.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Therefore, we can agree that this map is incomplete in terms that it does not fully reflect what is contained in the corrigendum to your summary, and that it should be -- should have also be corrected at the time when you were correcting your summary.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you are right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Mr. Janc, during your testimony on Friday, 30th of April, 2009 [as interpreted], and for my learned colleagues, that's on page 33520 and 521, in response to Ms. Soljan's question, you said that you were aware of the fact that three exhumations had been planned by the BH authorities in the near future. Do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: How do you know that three exhumations are planned to be conducted in the near future?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: During our -- my conversation with the members of the BiH institute on missing persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So your source are actually individuals from the Institute For Missing Persons of BiH who conveyed this directly to you; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Usually I call them, and then I ask them what is going on regarding the exhumations.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me specifically about these three planned exhumations mentioned on Friday. When did you have this conversation about the forthcoming exhumations?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say just recently, in last two or three weeks. I have called them twice, I guess. Yeah, twice. I was in contact with them twice, so ... perhaps three times, not more.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me if I say that for your work as an OTP investigator linked directly with this indictment, it is important for you to be familiar about the activities relating to the graves that are the subject of this indictment?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course, as much as I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: From your experience so far, and I think you said that you have been an OTP investigator since June 2006, were the Bosnia and Herzegovina authorities cooperative with the OTP concerning exhumations and other related activities?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can say they were cooperative, but very often very slow.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that the OTP of the ICTY had learned about the exhumations Hodzici Road 2 and Snagovo 3 conducted in September 2006 learned more than a year after the exhumation actually took place?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you then explain to me how do you know today about the planned exhumations when we see that the OTP was unaware of these above-mentioned exhumations for more than a year?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's a different story, because I have started close cooperation with this institute after my site visit in October 2007 when I learned about this Hodzici Road 2 exhumation, and I've seen at that time that we need regular contacts with them so in order to gain this information from them, so that's why this has changed after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So if I understood you correctly, although you started working in June 2006, this effort that you are currently making did not exist actually until 2007; i.e., there were no attempts to obtain information from the BH authorities concerning the planned or ongoing exhumations. Does that mean that before you started doing that, nobody did that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. There were attempts to do that, but probably there were not -- the methodology was different. I know that Dean Manning before was mainly dealing with these exhumations, and he was also in contacts with the BiH authorities regarding these exhumations, so and then he left, and in between this time -- in between, yeah, when he left and when I took over the position, there were probably -- there was probably lack of communication between us and BiH site regarding the exhumations.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Let us now move to the next topic. In your corrigendum dated the 9th of April, 2009, you say the following, that individual bodies from other locations apart from Kravica warehouse were also buried in the mass graves in Glogova. These other sites including following: The area in and around the Vuk Karadzic school in Bratunac, and in parenthesis, you said up to 80 bodies, according to W161, PW170, Desimir Dukanovic; the bases in Potocari according to PW170 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters didn't get the number of the bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry. I am going to continue where obviously we had a problem with the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. The interpreter didn't get the number of the bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So: "The area in and around Vuk Karadzic school in Bratunac, (up to 80 bodies according to PW161, PW170, and Desimir Dukanovic), the base in Potocari (6 to 7 bodies according to PW170), Konjevic Polje (10 to 15 bodies according to PW161), as well as the area along the Bratunac-Konjevic Polje road (1 truck-load of bodies collected according to PW161)."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Soljan.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, just one small detail for clarity of the record. It does not say base in Potocari but simply Potocari in the text. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you for that. We may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, I accept this correction provided by my learned friend Ms. Soljan. This is really not what is written in the corrigendum.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, in order to avoid any further misunderstanding, I would like to say outright to you that Mr. Borovcanin's Defence does not refute at all the fact that the bodies of the people who died in the incident in Kravica were indeed buried in the graves in Glogova. I would like just to discuss these bodies with you from other locations mentioned in your corrigendum, and I'm talking about the graves in Glogova. My first question is, according to what you know, what you included in your corrigendum, can we say that all the sites with the exception of the Kravica warehouse from where bodies were collected, were they buried in the graves in Glogova?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: We are now talking specifically about the Vuk Karadzic school, and it's mentioned in your corrigendum that there were 80 bodies. Among other things, you named Desimir Dukanovic as one of the sources. Since this Trial Chamber did not have an opportunity to hear Dukanovic's testimony, can you tell me more about this person, and why is he important for establishing this fact concerning the number of bodies? Why did you choose him particularly to include him in your corrigendum?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was interviewed by the BiH authorities, and also, I think he testified at the BiH state court, so he was personally involved in collecting the bodies from the Vuk Karadzic school and around the Vuk Karadzic school and transporting them to Glogova.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, would it be convenient to take a break now? I know we have five more minutes, but it's going to be a long quotation, and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, definitely by all means. Let's have a 25-minute break. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Janc, the last subject we discussed before the break was you giving us some details about Desimir Dukanovic and why he was significant enough for you to take his statement into account while making your corrigendum.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now look up in e-court 4D753. It is a record of witness interview for Desimir Dukanovic dated 20th March, 2007.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And you said something about this witness interview during your testimony. Can we move to page 4 in B/C/S, paragraph 5. And since we have no translation for this document, I will read out the relevant passage before I put a question to you. So for the transcript I'm reading from paragraph 5, the sentence beginning: "First, we collected the bodies from the Vuk Karadzic primary school, namely from the first room next to the entrance door on the right-hand side, six bodies; and from the second room, that is, classroom to the right from the entrance door, we picked up seven bodies. Upstairs in the school from the two classrooms located on the right-hand side looking from the entrance to the school with windows facing Vidovdanska Street, we picked up 10 to 15 bodies. After that, we collected more bodies from the lawn outside the school, which is located to the right of the entrance to the school, namely two bodies from just outside the entrance, two or three metres away. And further on, on the same green area facing the municipal building we picked up two more bodies, and then another four lying near the right-hand corner of the school facing the municipal building. "In addition, we collected also bodies from the green area on the right flank of the school looking from the entrance to the school, and there were 15 to 20 bodies there. From the left flank of the school next to the power transmission station we picked up six to seven bodies. After that we collected the bodies from the green area near the monument by the bazaar, and there were at least ten or so bodies there. "At the same time, I also saw a large number of bodies of Muslims killed on the playground, at least around 100. Those bodies we did not collect. I saw that those bodies on the playground were being collected by some people from Repovac, namely Mitar Kevic, who died after the war, and also brothers Sava and Ziko from Cerovac, who also died after the war. They were putting those bodies on the truck." I finished reading that passage from Mr. Dukanovic's statement that we believe to be of interested in relation to your corrigendum, and if I add it up correctly, all the bodies mentioned by Mr. Dukanovic in his statement, bodies found in Bratunac on various locations and buried in Glogova, it is at least 173 bodies. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct if you count also the last hundred bodies which are on the playground in Bratunac, although it is 73 of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Precisely. That's what I suggested can be seen from this statement. However, in your corrigendum, you say up to 180 bodies, and you invoke Desimir Dukanovic's statement as a source?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: 80 bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: But now when we read this statement, the number seems to be more than double the one quoted in your corrigendum?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's because of those 100 which I did not count because from his statement it's not clear where those bodies were taken. He is only talking about the bodies he picked it up, that they were taken to Glogova. And for these 100 bodies we don't know, as you can see from the statement, the people who picked them up are already dead. So but apart from that, I did not exclude the possibility that also those 100 bodies were taken to Glogova.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: That's precisely what I wanted to ask, but you anticipated my question. It is a very real possibility, indeed, in view of the time when this was happening, that these bodies, too, are to be found in Glogova 1 and 2.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the possibility is always there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Of course, and it's indeed very probable that these bodies were buried there, unless you have a different suggestion.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have different suggestion, so it can be the case, yes. But we don't have a clear indication or a statement from -- any statement showing that to be the fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [In English] All right. [Interpretation] You go on to say in the corrigendum that bodies from Potocari, Konjevic Polje, as well as a full truck-load of corpses collected on the Bratunac-Konjevic Polje Road were also buried there, and you refer to the testimony of PW161 in the corrigendum. I conclude, then, that you had occasion to read the testimony of PW161, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And then you know the fact that this witness said that in the graves in Glogova a certain number of bodies found in forests in the area of Ravni Buljim, Kamenica, and Pobudje were also buried. Are you aware of the fact that a testimony of the witness before this Tribunal includes that as well?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know he was testifying about the dead, but the conclusion can't be like you put it to me because I think later on like it was clarified with this same witness and he denied that would be the case in some way.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Let's clear up this dilemma first. I will quote to you exactly from the transcript; for my colleagues, it's on pages 9538 and 9538 [as interpreted] of the 27th March, 2007. I'll just make a short break for the interpreters to switch to English. [In English] "Q. And in these graves in Glogova, all the bodies that were found in Konjevic Polje were buried there too; isn't that correct? "A. Yes. "Q. But bodies found when searching the territory and the area of Ravni Buljim, Kamenica, Pobudje, these bodies were also buried there? "A. All those who were killed up there, and even the five or six bodies that I saw by the Vuk Karadzic school, the driver later informed me that there had been more of them. All of them have been taken and that" -- "to those graves and buried in those graves in Glogova. "Q. Glogova, or those graves in Glogova, where places where all these bodies were buried, this is at the location on the left" -- sorry. "A. This is a location on the left and the right to the road to Kravica, and what Momir said about the area in the direction of Halilovici, we weren't involved in that. I don't know who was." [Interpretation] Now, I finished quoting this first part of the testimony of PW161, and I'd like you to have a complete picture of what he said before I put my question. We are talking now about 9555, page 9555, the transcript of 27 March 2007, and page 9556. We start: [In English] "Q. Witness, are you aware of the area mentioned by Mr. Stojanovic called Ravni Buljim? "A. Ravni Buljim, I know where it is. "Q. Is that out in the woods beyond Jaglici in a rather remote area? "A. It's somewhere in the woods, and there are houses up there too. Ravni Buljim is a very wide area. "Q. During the days that we are talking about around the Kravica murder and afterward, did you, or anyone else you know, go back into those woods to retrieve Muslim bodies out of those woods? "A. Well, the employees of the public utilities company and the civilian protection gathered bodies. There were even lorries that couldn't access certain areas, but as to whether they were in Ravni Buljim, I don't know, but they did bring them in from the woods. "Q. Your people actually went into those woods at that time-frame with Muslim soldiers running around in those woods to pick up bodies. "A. No. That's not how it was done in the woods. It was up to the road, as far as the road, as far as the river, but as to the woods, as far as I know, given what I was told, on that day there were no soldiers, no Muslim soldiers." [Interpretation] So we've now familiarised ourselves with the entirety of what the witness had to say on this subject. I tried when quoting the transcript to present to you everything that this witness said on the subject, both in direct examination and in cross. At no point did the witness deny that the bodies from the woods were collected.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I was reading his testimony, I did understand a little bit different. And I don't see here, for example, when you are talking about Ravni Buljim that he is talking that these bodies are taken to Glogova. And I think when I was reviewing his testimony, that I did have different impression regarding these events. That's why I did not include them. I think you have to, you know, review his testimony again in its entirety. It's better than just going piece by piece.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Certainly, but you know his testimony was very long. There are hundreds of pages of transcript. These are the only references to the incident that I found. He is talking not only about Ravni Buljim, but also about Kamenica and Pobudje. That is a wider area. But let me ask you, do you deny that the bodies -- I'm not saying all bodies, and I cannot suggest that it's all bodies because there are surface remains, but can you exclude the possibility that part of the bodies that were closer and more accessible in the woods were in fact collected and buried?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I do not exclude this possibility. It's impossible to exclude these kind of possibilities.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And, of course, the same applies to Budak and Bljeceva that are relatively linked to this whole area.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand because Budak and Bljeceva are secondary graves. What is your exact question regarding this, that these bodies were taken directly to these graves? Is that your proposition?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: No, no, no. I'm not suggesting that. But you know yourself that the Budak grave is in a location where there had been burials even before the Kravica incident.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So Budak is partially a primary grave, not in relation to this, but Budak is a primary grave.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Actually, where secondary grave Budak one is located, there is a Muslim grave, yes, next to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Just one more question about this proposition that I made. It's a very reasonable possibility that those bodies were buried there, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which bodies you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I'm talking about the bodies collected in the woods, in the area we've just discussed, Buljim, Kamenica, Pobudje, and so on.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. If they were collected, those were buried somewhere for sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And the place which was the main site where all the bodies were buried is Glogova 1 and 2, in that area; right?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you are right. And the most of the work have been done by 17 according to aerial images of July, so in four days.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: All right. I promise to come back to this later on. We are still on the subject of PW161. Let me read to you another passage from his transcript. It's page 9392, lines 5 through 14,

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [In English] "Q. Okay. Can you give us a rough estimate, if you can, of how many bodies were buried in that grave?" [Interpretation] We are talking about Glogova of course. [In English] "A. The three days while I was down there and while people from the utilities company and the civilian protection were there, I think that between 4 and 500 bodies were buried. Also, I believe that other bodies were buried subsequently when I was no longer in the area. "Q. Okay. And do you have any idea about those? Did you get any reports of how many other bodies were buried at Glogova when you weren't there? "A. I don't know exactly." [Interpretation] So I've put to you another --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Soljan?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd ask that Mr. Lazarevic also reads to the witness the following two question-and-answers that follow that interchange, if possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: No problem, but my colleague will have to wait for a moment because I have it not in front of me, and I will do it in a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: No problem, I will quote.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Next question is: [In English] "Q. You testified on Friday that you assumed some of those bodies were from Kravica. Can you tell us more definitively what kind of knowledge, if any, you had about bodies from Kravica being buried in Glogova? "A. Well, most of the bodies buried in Glogova I believe were from Kravica because vehicles came from the direction of Kravica, and I know that people had been killed around the Zadruga Kravica, and those bodies were transported to Glogova. A FAP 13 lorry that was owned by the utilities company was involved in those activities." Do I need to go further?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Yes, please, one more question and answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: All right. "Q. It sounds like you've used the word that I haven't heard before. It may be a translation issue, but you said that the people had been killed around the something in Kravica. Can you tell us what you -- what you said? "A. I said that I believe that most of the people in -- who were buried in Glogova had been killed in Kravica because the lorries, one of which was FAP 13 lorry and was owned by the Rad utilities company in Bratunac, transported these bodies to the site in Glogova." [Interpretation] I hope -- [In English] [Previous translation continues]... I have no problem --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: She had said the next two questions and answers. You've read them out. So unless I hear any further, let's proceed then.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I think we've covered it all now and quoted the passages that are relevant. But based on what I've just read, we see that in the first three days - if we know that the incident in Kravica happened on the 13th, then we are talking about the 14th, 15th and 16th - after that incident between 400 and 500 bodies were buried in the grave in Glogova, including the bodies from the Vuk Karadzic school in Bratunac and from the road Bratunac-Konjevic Polje as well as bodies from Potocari. And after that, there were more burials in the Glogova grave, but Witness PW161 could not determine exactly on how many occasions bodies were buried or the exact number of bodies buried later. Can we agree that this is clear from the passage of the transcript that I quoted?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says there. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And bearing in mind that in your corrigendum you referred to the testimony of PW161, I believe that the information and testimony he provided here have certain weight in relation to the Prosecution case; correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Also on the subject, did you have occasion to review the report about exhumations in Glogova 2 site prepared by Mr. Jose-Pablo Baraybar. You had occasion to read this report?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I did review this report.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now look up in e-court P2475. That's the report by Mr. Baraybar, and we need page 14 in B/C/S, which is page 19 in English. And while we are waiting for that page to be displayed in e-court, I'd like to look at the paragraph that starts with the words "another interesting point ..." So can you see this lower part which begins with "another interesting point ..."? We can see it in English, as well, and it reads as follows: "Another interesting point to discuss is the fact that the grave GL02-09 consists of a string of graves of various dimensions. This implies that graves of different sizes were being excavated according to the needs to dispose bodies therein and that there may have been a relative time difference between the excavation of each of the graves. At this point, it is not possible to precise what was the absolute 'time' difference between each of the burial episodes." Can you see that in front of you? And do you agree that this is what Mr. Baraybar's report reads?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see and I can agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now that we have read this passage, is it consistent with what Witness PW161 said and that we read a minute ago, that is to say that there were several burials at different times, which is also clear from the forensic evidence?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we can say something like that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you very much. The next thing that I would like to ask you about is during your work for the ICTY OTP, did you have an opportunity to familiarise yourself with the fact that in the very town of Srebrenica there were a number of people who were killed and that the bodies were in the town of Srebrenica itself? Did you know about that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember these bodies. They are also on footages, I think, on videos. You can see them, some of them, so I'm aware of this fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, you are absolutely right, and that can be seen. I would like to ask you whether you know where these bodies from the town of Srebrenica were buried. Did you ever come across such piece of information? Where is their burial site?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't have any information on these bodies so far.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And, of course, you cannot rule out the possibility that given where they were found, probably ended up in Glogova 1 or 2 being the closest ones where the bodies were buried immediately after the fall of Srebrenica, at least the majority of the bodies?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's possible, you know, but that would be speculation because I haven't seen any evidence regarding these particular bodies so far, where they ended up.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Of course I agree, and if it were possible, I would gladly show you the evidence about where these bodies ended, but we cannot reasonably rule out the possibility that they were buried in Glogova; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: In your corrigendum, you say that of the total number of bodies found in Glogova, 12 bodies need to be excluded that had been found in a Glogova L grave. There is evidence for ten victims that they had been brought from Serbia on the 20th, the 24th, and 26th of July, 1995. Do you remember that portion of your corrigendum?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: The next question is, are you aware of the fact that in his report, Professor Richard Wright stated that the grave Glogova L was excavated in the period between 17th and 27th July, 1995? I assume that together with the documents that you cited in the corrigendum was the reason for you to remove these bodies from the possible number of victims in Kravica. Did you take into account the findings of Professor Richard Wright?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, can we please look at P674, page 20 in B/C/S and page 22 in the English version. That's the report of Professor Richard Wright of 9 February 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: When we come to the relevant page, I would like you to focus on item C somewhere in the middle of the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So we need pages 20 and 22 in B/C/S and English respectively. Can we scroll down the page in B/C/S so that we can see item C.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: It reads that by 27th of July, 1995, but in order for you to understand the context, that means the period between the 17th and the 27th of July, 1995, graves E and L had been added to the bottom western section of the suspect area. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that, and I'm very well aware of this fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So it is obvious from this that not only grave L mentioned by you in the corrigendum but also grave E was excavated at a later date; is that correct? Actually, we have two subgraves within Glogova 1; right?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you are right. But for grave L, we know that who those individuals are and where they are coming from. For grave E, we don't have such example.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let us summarise what you have said. In your corrigendum, you exclude grave L for three reasons. The first reason was that there were no documents supporting that the people found there had been alive on the 16th, 20th, and 26th of July; secondly, because there are some specific features such as ligatures that were not characteristic of other graves in Glogova; and thirdly, because you relied on Mr. Richard Wright's report which says that they were excavated at a later date. Did I cite all the reasons?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was the case. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So in order for you to see grave L, let's move to page 15 in B/C/S and page 16 in English. However, what is common for both graves E and L is that they were excavated in the same period, i.e., after the main burial testified to by Witness PW161. I'm sorry. For transcript I have to make a correction. I'm talking about grave E now, and we can see that it talks about six bodies; right?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, right. And this is I think the only similarity you have between those two graves. All the rest is different.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes. But regardless of that, there is something that links these two graves, and that is that they were excavated after the main burial took place testified about by Witness PW161 when the bodies from Kravica had already been buried.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree with you. But for grave E, the importance of this grave is that inside this grave you have the artifacts from Kravica warehouse, so this is coming out of Michael Hedley's report, and you will see that you have artifacts from Kravica warehouse. So inside this grave are the bodies which were most probably buried or taken from Kravica. That's the difference. But in grave L, you don't have any of such artifacts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, yes, but of course you cannot rule out the possibility of the contamination of the grave, that is to say that the same machines used -- were used and they could have contaminated the graves E as well.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, if we can take a break now, I'm about to move to another topic. This is a very long one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: How long? How much more do you reckon you need.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Honestly speaking, I believe one hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Janc, we are going to stop here today. We will continue tomorrow morning, thank you, at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
